sentences.text: This present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been filed against the award dated 26.08.2015, passed in Claim Case No.714/2015 by 3rd Additional MACT, Indore.
By the said award, learned Tribunal partly allowed the claim case and granted compensation to the tune of Rs.15,10,000/- along with the interest of 6% per annum.
2. Factual matrix of the case are that on 24.01.2014 Jitendra was going Rasalpur on a motorcycle.

When he reached Rasalpur Bypass Square at the same respondent No.1 who was driving the motorcycle bearing registration No.MP-41-MD-1905 rashly and negligently and dashed the deceased, as a result of which Jitendra suffered severe injuries and during the treatment he died.
The appellant claimants filed a claim petition for a compensation of Rs.40,00,000/-.

3. Learned MACT after appreciating the evidence on record, partly NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:3592 2 MA-1697-2015 allowed the claim and awarded a sum of Rs.15,10,000/-
against the claim of Rs.40,00,000/-.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that learned tribunal has not properly assessed the amount of compensation granted to the appellant.
No amount under the head of future prospects has been awarded and therefore, he prays for enhancement in the compensation.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent refuting the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the finding arrived at by the learned tribunal are just and proper and does not require any interference by this Court in this appeal.
6. I have heard the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

Smt. Sangitabai vs Haider Patel on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195860658/
1 7.
It is not in dispute that respondent No.1 was responsible for causing the accident and the offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.3/Insurance Company.
The only question for determination in this appeal is that whether the amount awarded by the Tribunal requires modification or not?.

8. Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for parties, this Court finds that the learned Tribunal erred while passing the impugned award and thus the compensation is being reassessed as under :

Annual Income : Rs.1,87,386/-
Rs.187386 x 1/4 = Rs.46,846/-
Rs.1,87,386 - Rs.46,846/- = Rs.1,40,539/- Future Prospects (40%) : Rs.1,40,539 +
Rs.56,215x 17 (multiplier) = Rs.33,44,818/-
Consortium Rs.2,80,000/- (Rs.40,000/- x 7) NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:3592 3 MA-1697-2015 Funeral Expenses = Rs.15,000/-
Loss of Estate = Rs.15,000/-
Total amount = Rs.36,54,818/-
Rs.36,54,818 x 60% (contributory negligence) = Rs.21,92,890.8/- Round off =
Rs.21,92,890/-
Rs.21,92,890 - Rs.15,10,000/- (already awarded by the Tribunal) = Rs.6,82,890 (enhanced amount)
9.
Accordingly, the claimant is entitled to the get the compensation to the tune of Rs.21,92,890/- in place of Rs.15,10,000/-.

The enhanced sum of Rs.6,82,890/- (Rs.21,92,890 - Rs.15,10,000/-) shall carry the same interest as has been awarded by the learned Tribunal subject to following conditions:-
"i.
The respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order, failing which the execution can be taken out against him.
ii. The claimant is directed to pay the requisite Court Fee, if required in the present case.
iii. On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the amount with accrued interest and costs, by filing a proper application before the Tribunal.
iv. The record be sent back to the learned Tribunal within three weeks from this day.
v. As a sequel, interlocutory applications pending consideration, if any, shall stand closed.

2 vi.
No order as to costs.
(HIMANSHU JOSHI) JUDGE (ra)
